title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: design custom AI agents with the AI development toolkit
summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly implies that custom agents can run only from manually created tasks, although Microsoft explicitly allows developer-built triggers. The capacity path omits its card, and the allocation API entry needs an actual request body rather than a description of its fields.

claims.claim: The printed PUT allocation call with a prose list of body fields is a usable API allocation request.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Platform Copilot Credits licensing allocationsV2 scope environmentId MCSMessages enforcementRules TenantPool. Opened allocation tutorial: endpoint, PUT and version exist, but the printed entry supplies no request body or values for environmentId and quantity.
claims.fix: Keep the endpoint and docs URL, but replace the call with 'PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01; Content-Type: application/json; body: {"scope":{"environmentId":"<environment-id>"},"allocatedEntitlements":[{"entitlementId":"MCSMessages","allocation":{"quantity":<credits>},"enforcementRules":[{"ruleType":"TenantPool","enabled":false}]}]}'. The environment-id and credits tokens are placeholders to replace before sending the request. This is the tutorial's documented allocation shape; the endpoint's absence from the deterministic literal-string search was not evidence that it did not exist.

claims.quote: An app registration configured for Power Platform API. Note the app registration's application (client) ID and directory (tenant) ID.

claims.claim: The TenantPool rule maps to Draw from the available capacity in my tenant and permits unallocated tenant-pool usage when enabled.
claims.quote: The Draw from the available capacity in my tenant option in the admin center maps to the TenantPool enforcement rule: when it's enabled, the environment continues to draw from unallocated tenant capacity after its own allocation is exhausted

claims.where: controls[3].note; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Disabling TenantPool alone caps the environment at its allocation.
claims.quote: when it's disabled, the environment is capped at its allocation.
claims.fix: Qualify the cap advice: 'The allocation tutorial describes disabling TenantPool as capping the environment. The capacity-management page also permits pay-as-you-go overages and says the allocation is a cap only if no overage source is enabled; clear both Draw from the available capacity in my tenant and Bill to my pay-as-you-go billing plan for that cap.' The second source is https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/manage-copilot-studio-copilot-credits-capacity.

claims.quote: Updates through the Power Platform admin center, Power Platform API, or administration SDKs are rejected with the TenantPoolLockedByPolicy error.

claims.quote: Some AI features take effect immediately, while others require users to sign out and sign in again.

claims.where: Governance guidance versus Governance controls table

claims.fix: The human design/diagnostic permission assignments, consumption monitoring, and export/backup steps have no corresponding control rows. Keep this as an editorial coverage finding; do not add unverified rows as part of this correction.

claims.claim: The roadmap recommends keeping exported agent definitions in source control such as GitHub.
claims.quote: We recommend storing these files in a source control system like GitHub to track changes and maintain version history.
